text:
sasha: midday heads-up — canary on quant-kernel v1.3.2 is showing transient p95 spikes (~450ms -> 1.2s) for long-seq requests. not universal, small slice (3%) but repeats across two hosts.

mike: saw that in graphs, looks like KV cache eviction thrash at ~120s. memory climbs then drops and latency follows.

anya: is this the build with the new fused-matmul kernel? we rolled that earlier this morning.

mike: yes, fused-matmul + new allocator path. suspect allocator heuristics + quant layout. low sample but consistent.

deploybot: deploybot: Started canary rollout: quant-kernel v1.3.2 -> 1000 reqs (3% traffic) on pool-runtime-canary-us-west at 2012-03-21T12:34:56Z

kevin: reprod attempt on staging failed to reproduce locally. need a longer-run smoke on canary hosts. spinning up a 30m soak.

sasha: ok, let's not escalate to rollback yet. plan: 1) pin high-traffic customers off v1.3.2 (if hit) 2) extend canary soak to 1h 3) gather allocation traces and logs.

anya: +1. i'll prepare the allocation trace capture and enable hotprof on those canary VMs.

mike: i'll add a temporary routing rule to pin customer-ids [acct_77, acct_212] to v1.2 for the next 2h — they showed >1.0s p95.

sasha: perfect. mike, post the exact deploybot command you used for pinning.

mike: ran: `/deploy pin --route pool-runtime-canary-us-west --model quant-kernel:v1.2 --customers acct_77,acct_212 --ttl 2h`

deploybot: deploybot: Route update successful. pinned acct_77, acct_212 -> quant-kernel:v1.2 (TTL 2h)

oncall-bot: oncall-bot: alert suppressed for p95 spike (alert 4521) while team investigating — will re-enable after 2h or on manual clear.

anya: capture snippet i'm collecting:```
alloc_trace: [2021-10-12T12:36:01Z] host-08: alloc 1.2GB (matmul_buffer)
alloc_trace: [2021-10-12T12:36:02Z] host-08: free 1.2GB
alloc_trace: [2021-10-12T12:36:04Z] host-08: high alloc churn detected
```

mike: thanks. that looks like churn aligning with p95 jumps. can you also grab `dmesg` / OOM logs?

anya: copying logs to /shared/eng-runtime/2012345678/ — will be zipped in 20m. link: https://files.redwood.internal/eng-runtime/2012345678/logs.zip

sasha: if allocator heuristics are the culprit, quick mitigation is to revert allocator tweak in v1.3.3 build and roll that out as v1.3.4. dev cycle ~1h. decision time: do we pin and wait, or produce v1.3.4 and rollforward?

kevin: dev has a small fix ready — changes allocator threshold back to previous value and adds extra guard. i can build and smoke in 30–40m.

mike: prefer rollforward with patch (v1.3.4) if testing passes. less customer-facing churn than a full rollback.

sasha: agreed. start build and include a quick perf microbenchmark. keep canary slice paused until we have build smoke.

kevin: starting build now. will push artifact to registry when ready: `registry.redwood/quant-kernel:v1.3.4-hotfix`

deploybot: deploybot: build pipeline triggered for registry.redwood/quant-kernel:v1.3.4-hotfix (CI-9423)

anya: continuing trace capture during build. keep pinned customers on v1.2.

kevin: build done, pushed. smoke run on canary host returned stable p95 ~420ms for 30m run. no alloc churn captured.

mike: nice. canary team — ready to roll to canary slice? we should still start with 3% then step to 10% after 30m.

sasha: yes. deploybot, schedule staged rollout: 3% -> 10% -> 25% with 30m waits. abort on p95 > 800ms or error rate > 0.5%.

deploybot: deploybot: Scheduled staged rollout for registry.redwood/quant-kernel:v1.3.4-hotfix on pool-runtime-canary-us-west. steps: 3% (start), 10% (30m), 25% (30m). Abort conditions set.

mike: rolling now to 3%. monitoring dashboards on: eng-runtime/canary/quant-kernel-v1.3.4-hotfix

sasha: monitoring looks clean at +10m. p95 stable, GPU mem flat. proceeding to 10% in 20m.

anya: allocation traces for v1.3.4 look clean — no repeated alloc/free. attaching quick diff: https://files.redwood.internal/eng-runtime/2012345678/alloc-diff.txt

mike: after 10% hold, if still stable we'll open release notes draft and schedule a minor release entry: "v1.3.4: allocator heuristics hotfix, addresses transient latency in long-sequence quantized workloads"

sasha: good. mike, can you create the release note PR and include rollback triggers + mitigations?

mike: on it. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2314 — draft with metrics and rollback steps.

deploybot: deploybot: Staged rollout advanced to 10% at 2012-03-21T13:05:12Z

oncall-bot: oncall-bot: Alert channel re-enabled for p95 spike (alert 4521) — will notify on breach.

kevin: 10% hold looks fine. advancing to 25%.

sasha: once 25% holds for 30m, schedule a non-urgent deploy to dedicated pools overnight (low-traffic window) and then to prod. we'll keep pinned TTL for the two high-traffic customers until full prod rollout completes.

anya: will follow up with an ops runbook entry capturing the capture steps for future repros.

mike: release note PR created and assigned to sasha for sign-off.

sasha: signing off now. thanks team — great coordinated rollforward. i'll close the thread after prod rollout. :tada:

mike: thanks. i'll unpin the TTL once prod rollout completes and monitor edges.

deploybot: deploybot: Staged rollout reached 25% at 2012-03-21T13:38:32Z; no aborts.

sasha: last_message: prod rollout scheduled 02:00 UTC tonight, release notes merged. follow-ups: postmortem only if we see regressions in next 48h.

kevin: noted. arch ticket created: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/RUNTIME-482 — tracking allocator heuristic change for next major cleanup.

mike: thanks all.
